summary: Honour declared terminal outcomes and skip ignored runtime trees

delivery.outcome: Terminal lease release honours every policy-declared terminal outcome, version parity ignores git-ignored runtime trees, and writer-check accepts the canonical lease repository identity.
nonGoals: No change to review, approval, publication or merge authority.
No weakening of ancestry, fencing, phase or ownership checks.
No release/version bump and no consumer adoption in this ticket.

architecture.decision: Take the terminal outcome from the managed ticket-activity policy instead of a hardcoded name; enumerate version-parity candidates through git ls-files -co --exclude-standard with the previous glob as a non-Git fallback; accept either the canonical owner/name identity written by the allocator or the legacy local digest in writer-check. Bundled validator copies stay byte-identical and delivery verification stays ancestry-bound.
interfaceChanges: writer-check accepts the canonical owner/name lease identity in addition to the legacy local digest; foreign actors and repositories still refuse.
architecture.rollback: Independently reviewed revert; preserve the ticket branch and adopted releases.

validation.evidence: A no-change receipt releases a claimed lease through cancel then release.
Undeclared outcomes, foreign owners, stale fences and dirty worktrees still refuse.
Ignored runtime trees are skipped while a tracked mismatching initializer is still reported.
Lease checking loads from the validator package; hub and bundled copies stay identical.
Canonical governance gates pass on the ticket head.
Canonical owner/name lease identity is accepted while foreign actors still refuse.
